title: FBISE Section A Board Examination Simulator 02 (Tenses, Agreement & Verbals)
subject: english-10

questions.question: Identify the tense: 'By next June, he will have been working in this firm for ten years.'
questions.explanation: 'will have been working' with a time duration ('for ten years') and a future reference point ('by next June') exemplifies the Future Perfect Continuous tense.

questions.question: Choose the correct verb form: 'Neither of the boys ___ present in the classroom yesterday.'
questions.explanation: The distributive pronoun 'neither' is singular and takes a singular verb ('was') when referring to past time.

questions.question: Identify the type of verb in: 'The child seems unhappy today.'
questions.explanation: 'Seems' links the subject 'the child' with the subject complement adjective 'unhappy'; therefore, it functions as a linking (copular) verb.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences contains an INTRANSITIVE verb?

options.A: The author wrote an inspiring story.
options.B: The birds fly high in the sky.
options.D: She baked delicious cookies for us.

questions.explanation: 'Fly' in 'The birds fly high' does not take a direct object ('high in the sky' is an adverbial prepositional modifier), making it intransitive.

questions.question: Choose the correct verb form: 'Mathematics ___ considered a foundational discipline for engineers.'
questions.explanation: Nouns denoting academic subjects ending in '-ics' (Mathematics, Physics, Economics, Civics) are plural in form but take a singular verb ('is').

questions.question: Identify the tense: 'When I entered the room, the speaker had already delivered his speech.'
questions.explanation: 'entered' is Past Simple, describing the subsequent action, while 'had delivered' is Past Perfect, representing the anterior completed action.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence following the rule of proximity in subject-verb agreement:

options.A: Either the captain or the players are responsible for the victory.
options.B: Either the captain or the players is responsible for the victory.
options.C: Either the players or the captain are responsible for the victory.
options.D: Neither the teacher nor the students was present.

questions.explanation: When subjects are joined by 'either...or' / 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the subject closest to it. 'Players' is plural, so 'are' is correct.

questions.question: Complete the sentence with the correct tense: 'They ___ in this city since 2015.'
questions.explanation: An action that began in the past and continues into the present marked with 'since [year]' requires the Present Perfect Continuous tense ('have been living').

questions.question: Identify the underlined verbal: '*Swimming* is an excellent full-body exercise.'
questions.explanation: 'Swimming' functions as the grammatical subject of the sentence (acting as a verbal noun), which defines a Gerund.

questions.question: In which sentence is the underlined word a PRESENT PARTICIPLE functioning as an ADJECTIVE?

options.A: I saw a *flying* bird across the valley.
options.C: He is tired of *waiting* in queues.

questions.explanation: In 'a flying bird', 'flying' modifies the noun 'bird' as an adjective, functioning as a present participle.

questions.question: Identify the verbal: 'The *broken* vase could not be repaired.'
questions.explanation: 'Broken' is the V3 form of 'break' functioning adjectivally to describe the noun 'vase', which is a Past Participle.

questions.question: Identify the verbal in: 'She made me *laugh* out loud.'
questions.explanation: Causative verbs like 'make' (here past 'made') take an object followed by a bare infinitive (an infinitive without 'to': 'laugh').

questions.question: Identify the function of the underlined gerund: 'He was punished for *lying*.'

options.C: Direct object of a transitive verb

questions.explanation: 'Lying' follows the preposition 'for' and serves as its object (object of a preposition).

questions.question: Identify the verbal: 'I heard the baby *crying* in the nursery.'
questions.explanation: 'Crying' describes the condition/action of 'the baby' (acting as an objective complement participle), hence it is a present participle.

questions.question: In which sentence does an INFINITIVE express PURPOSE?

options.A: He went to the library to study in silence.
options.B: To err is human, to forgive divine.
options.C: Her dream is to travel around the globe.
options.D: I want to buy a new bicycle.

questions.explanation: 'To study in silence' answers 'Why did he go to the library?' functioning as an adverbial infinitive of purpose.
